name: Seared Sirloin with Roasted Potatoes & Broccoli
subtitle: One sheet pan of potatoes and broccoli, steak in a skillet
equipment: 1 sheet pan, heavy skillet (cast iron if you have it), thermometer

macros.portion: About 7½ oz cooked steak, 1¾ cups roasted potatoes and 1½ cups broccoli.
macros.note: Rough estimate from standard nutrition values for the listed amounts, not a lab number.

before: Salt the steak as soon as you turn on the oven. The extra 30 min seasons it through and dries the surface for a better crust.
notes: The broccoli joins the potatoes partway through so both finish together on one pan. Pull the steak at 125–130°F for medium-rare; it rises a few degrees while it rests. USDA's minimum for steak is 145°F with a 3-minute rest.

steps.title: Oven on, steak salted
steps.body: Put an **empty sheet pan** on the middle rack and heat the oven to 425°F. Pat **1¼ lb sirloin** dry and season both sides with **1 tsp kosher salt + ½ tsp pepper**. Leave it on a plate.

steps.title: Potatoes in
steps.body: Halve **1½ lb baby potatoes**. In a large bowl, toss with **1 Tbsp olive oil + ¾ tsp salt + ¼ tsp pepper + 1 tsp garlic powder**. Spread on the hot pan, cut sides down. Roast **20 min**.

steps.title: Ready the broccoli
steps.body: While the potatoes roast, toss **1 lb broccoli florets** in the same bowl with **2 tsp olive oil + ¼ tsp salt**. Set out the skillet, tongs, thermometer and a cutting board.

steps.title: Broccoli in
steps.body: Flip the potatoes and push them to one side. Spread the broccoli on the other side in one layer. Roast **15–18 min**, until the potatoes are deep golden and the broccoli edges char.

steps.title: Sear the steak
steps.body: Right after the broccoli goes in: skillet over medium-high for **3 min**. Add **1 tsp neutral oil**, then the steak. Sear **4 min** without moving it, flip, and sear **3–5 min** more until the thickest point reads 125–130°F.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.body: Rest the steak on the board **5 min**. Pull the sheet pan. Slice the steak thin against the grain and serve with the potatoes and broccoli.
